What we do
01

Content & film

Films, campaigns, and imagery for brands and houses, produced through custom pipelines that let us move faster and hold a higher frame.

02

Spatial & immersive

Photoreal environments, installations, and built worlds. Rendered before they exist, and made to be entered.

03

Games & IP

Game ready environments, characters, and assets. Original playable IP and collectible characters, licensable to studios and platforms.

04

Production & tech

3D, procedural craft, and the pipelines behind the work. Architectural precision, generative method.

Our production is powered by custom AI and generative pipelines, built in house and directed to a brand standard.

Lab · Research and development

What we own,
and what we're building.

The studio builds its own engines and its own worlds. This is the inventory — what runs in production today, what is in development, and what is still research.

Scroll ↓
01 / 07  ·  Lab
Why the Lab exists

Most studios rent their capability. We build ours — which is why a campaign's worth of variants costs what one shoot used to, and why the IP we make stays yours.

[ studio still · 4:5 ]
02 / 07  ·  Lab
How the work is made
03 / 07  ·  Lab
Engines and tools
AI production pipelinesIn production

Generative pipelines assembled and directed in house, tuned per sector rather than one general-purpose model doing everything badly.

Procedural character systemIn production

Builds procedural characters and exports them across formats, so one character drops into a game engine, a render pipeline or a garment workflow without being rebuilt for each.

Procedural art, environments and spacesIn production

Art, environments and spaces generated from rules rather than modelled by hand — which is how a world gets built at a scale hand-modelling cannot reach.

CLONE EngineIn development

Build once, generate endlessly. A single master build becomes a campaign's worth of variants across ratios, channels and markets, without a reshoot.

Asset libraryIn development

A growing library of production-ready assets, built once and reused across projects rather than remade from scratch each time.

[ engine capture · 16:9 ]

The engines, procedural systems and asset library the studio builds for its own production, rather than whatever you can afford alone.

Paid commissions

When work comes in that matches your discipline, members get called first. The training is the route in, not the product.

A network that teaches itself

The Collective runs as a peer group. Members review each other's work, share methods and pass on what they learn — the studio is one voice in it, not the only one.

Commissioned project work

Ongoing production runs

The hub

The talent database

Every member is logged by discipline, toolset and availability. When a brief lands, the studio searches the database rather than starting a hiring round — which is why membership converts into work.

Learning sideways

Members run reviews and share methods with each other. A game developer explains engine constraints to a 3D artist; the artist shows what the pipeline can actually produce. That exchange is the point.

Based at Yas Creative Hub

The studio sits inside the Abu Dhabi media and gaming cluster, so the Collective trains into a real local industry rather than into a vacuum.
